name: Resupply USD
oneLiner: REUSD is Resupply's CDP stablecoin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares (crvUSD/frxUSD); a 1% communal-redemption fee sets a price floor.
collateral: crvUSD and frxUSD lending vault tokens from Curve Lend and Fraxlend
pegMechanism: Communal redemption model with 1% fee establishing a price floor; borrow rate is the higher of half the lending rate, half the sfrxUSD rate, or 2%; underlying collateral depends on crvUSD/frxUSD ecosystems which rely on centralized stablecoin peg keepers

oracleRisk.summary: Resupply lending pairs value ERC-4626 collateral from its share-to-underlying conversion while treating the crvUSD or frxUSD underlying as one dollar, so liquidations use an internal vault-rate path rather than market-price feeds.

branchApplicability.rationale: reUSD is borrowed through separately registered Curve Lend and Fraxlend collateral pairs. At Ethereum block 25530458, 18 registered pairs pointed to the same BasicVaultOracle and shared ResupplyPair, LiquidationHandler, and InsurancePool logic; the wstUSR pair had a zero oracle and zero borrow limit. The configured pairs are therefore represented as one grouped common-engine branch and wstUSR is excluded.

branches.label: Registered Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault pairs
branches.summary: Enabled Resupply pairs use the common BasicVaultOracle to convert lending-vault shares to crvUSD or frxUSD units and apply the pair's configured maximum LTV without an external USD market-price feed.
collateralAssets: Registered Curve Lend and Fraxlend ERC-4626 vault shares backed by crvUSD or frxUSD

feeds.path: ERC-4626 convertToAssets share rate, with crvUSD/frxUSD treated as $1 -> inverted pair exchange rate -> borrower LTV

branches.fallbackBehavior: The pair calls BasicVaultOracle on every exchange-rate update and stores a new rate only when the result changes. A reverting vault conversion or out-of-bounds share price reverts the operation; the liquidation path does not fall back to the stored exchange rate or an external stablecoin market feed.

collateralParameters.asset: Registered Curve Lend and Fraxlend ERC-4626 vault shares backed by crvUSD or frxUSD
collateralParameters.note: The deployment default is 95% maximum LTV, but governance can configure maximum LTV, borrow limit, and liquidation fee per registered pair.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When current debt divided by vault-share value exceeds the pair maximum LTV, any caller may route a liquidation through LiquidationHandler. The pair closes the borrower's full debt, transfers collateral shares to the handler, and pays the configured liquidation incentive from recovered collateral where available.
branches.backstop: LiquidationHandler redeems recovered vault shares into the Resupply InsurancePool and burns InsurancePool reUSD assets up to both recovered value and the pool's burnable balance.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Any portion not covered by redeemable collateral or the InsurancePool remains recorded as debtByCollateral. Governance can later process collateral and clear that debt when the InsurancePool can burn it; the guardian pause sets pair borrowing capacity to zero but does not define a global settlement or alternate oracle.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified REUSD source exposes owner/operator-controlled mint and standard ERC-20 transfers, but no holder blacklist, freeze, seizure, or global pause function. The owner is Resupply Core and proposal execution is governed by the token-weighted Voter with a seven-day vote and one-day execution delay. crvUSD and frxUSD lending-vault collateral create upstream loss exposure without granting their controllers access to REUSD holder balances.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: REUSD mint() requires operators[msg.sender] || msg.sender == owner(). No direct REUSD operators have been set, and owner() returns the Core contract (0xc07e…), Resupply's on-chain governance hub. Core.execute() is callable by the Voter contract (0x1111…), a token-weighted on-chain governance contract requiring quorum, a voting period, and execution delay; bounded Guardian operator permissions remain active for emergency actions but do not grant direct stablecoin mint access.

mintIncidents.summary: Resupply's crvUSD/wstUSR market exploit manipulated exchange-rate and solvency logic so negligible collateral could borrow up to the reUSD debt limit, leaving bad debt through the stablecoin borrow route.

controls.label: REUSD owner — Resupply Core governance contract
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25321527: owner() on REUSD returned 0xc07e000044f95655c11fda4cd37f70a94d7e0a7d. eth_getCode returned contract code. REUSD source: mint() requires operators[msg.sender] || msg.sender == owner(); no direct REUSD operator was found in the reviewed state. Core source: execute() is callable by voter 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6 (token-weighted on-chain governance) or operators with explicit per-selector permissions. Active GuardianUpgradeable permissions are bounded emergency/operator functions rather than direct stablecoin mint authority.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25321527: REUSD mint() is gated by owner (Core 0xc07e…) or direct stablecoin operators; Core.voter() returns 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6. The Voter contract enforces token-weighted proposal execution with 30% quorum, a 7-day voting period, and a 1-day execution delay. Resupply's docs state contracts are owned by Core and governed through on-chain voting. The current GuardianUpgradeable proxy is controlled by a 3-of-5 Safe and has bounded emergency/operator permissions, but the active implementation does not expose the older revertVoter path and does not hold direct REUSD mint authority. Mint authority is therefore DAO-governed with emergency multisig controls. reUSD minting is over-collateralised issuance gated by owner (the Resupply Core governance contract) or explicitly set operators; at block 25321527 Core execution is controlled by the token-weighted Voter contract enforcing a 30% quorum, a 7-day voting period and a 1-day execution delay, so authorising new mint capacity requires on-chain governance behind an independently enforced delay. The encoding-derived direct-mint cap is therefore economically raiseable rather than unbounded, placing reUSD outside the fiat-custodial centralized-mint scope.
review.reviewer: Codex governance review; Claude SOL-V mint-tier mop-up

sources.label: Resupply Registry and pair accounting on Ethereum

reserveReview.rationale: The independent resupply-pairs producer enumerated every configured positive-collateral pair and converted its ERC-4626 shares at the same on-chain capture. Aggregating by underlying produced 94% Curve crvUSD lending-market exposure and 6% Fraxlend frxUSD lending-market exposure. Both are layered protocol positions whose upstream issuer and smart-contract failure domains remain explicit.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Exact live Resupply pair registry and ERC-4626 collateral conversion captured on 2026-07-15
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: No positive-collateral pair is omitted; vault liquidity, borrower collateral, and upstream crvUSD or frxUSD solvency remain structured risk factors within the two classified positions.

notices.title: June 2025 exploit was repaid
notices.message: Resupply suffered a June 2025 oracle-manipulation exploit that created about $9.6M of bad debt. The protocol reported the bad debt fully repaid by August 2025 using treasury funds, insurance-pool burn mechanics, and a Yearn DAO loan, but the incident remains relevant to vault/oracle risk.
